question: I made some uncommitted edits but need to switch tasks without losing them or committing — what lets me set them aside temporarily?
expected_answer: It temporarily shelves uncommitted changes so you can switch tasks and reapply them later.

question: What capability does a reviewer get before someone elses proposed code changes actually get merged in?
expected_answer: Comment on proposed changes before they are merged.

question: If I want a straight-line history with no merge bumps instead of combining two branches with a two-parent commit, what should I use instead?
expected_answer: Rebase rewrites history to produce a linear sequence of commits onto a new base; merge creates a new commit with two parents instead.

question: When the same part of a file was edited two different ways on two branches being combined, what problem occurs?
expected_answer: It happens when the same lines of a file are changed differently in two branches being merged.

question: What is my own personal copy of somebody elses repository called, living under my own account?
expected_answer: A personal copy of someone elses repository in your own account.

question: Which file tells version control to ignore certain build outputs or secret files so they never get tracked?
expected_answer: It lists file and directory patterns that Git should not track.

question: What technique finds the exact commit that introduced a regression by repeatedly narrowing down the history?
expected_answer: It performs a binary search through commit history to find the commit that introduced a bug.

question: What unique fingerprint identifies one exact snapshot of a repositorys state?
expected_answer: A SHA-1 checksum that uniquely identifies a specific snapshot of the repository.

question: Whats the difference between undoing a change by adding a new opposite commit versus just moving the branch pointer backward?
expected_answer: Revert creates a new commit undoing a previous change without rewriting history; reset moves the branch pointer and can rewrite history.

question: If I check out an individual commit instead of a named branch, what unusual state does my repo end up in?
expected_answer: It occurs when you check out a specific commit instead of a branch so new commits belong to no branch.

question: What practice automatically builds and runs tests every time someone pushes new code?
expected_answer: It automatically builds and tests code whenever changes are pushed.

question: Which file automatically assigns specific people or teams as reviewers whenever certain parts of the codebase change?
expected_answer: It specifies which people or teams are automatically requested to review changes to certain files.

question: In a versioning scheme like 2.5.1, what does changing the very first number signal to users?
expected_answer: A MAJOR version bump means a breaking change to compatibility.

question: Where would I look to see a running history of notable changes across each released version of a project?
expected_answer: A file recording notable changes made to a project in each release.

question: What system lets end users report problems and ask for new capabilities, which maintainers then prioritize?
expected_answer: It lets users report bugs and request features and lets maintainers triage and prioritize work.

question: What do you call an automated YAML-defined workflow that fires off when someone pushes code or opens a review request?
expected_answer: An automated workflow defined in YAML that runs in response to events like pushes or pull requests.

question: Before merging in a messy branch, whats the term for collapsing many small commits down into just one?
expected_answer: Combining multiple commits into a single commit; often used to clean up history before merging.

question: Whats the label on a commit that marks it as an official release point, like v1.0.0?
expected_answer: It marks a specific commit; commonly used for release points.

question: What do you call the original source repository that someone elses copy was branched off from?
expected_answer: The original repository that a fork was created from.

question: If I only want to download new remote changes without blending them into my current branch automatically, what command should I use instead of the one that does both?
expected_answer: Fetch downloads new data from a remote without merging it into local branches; pull merges automatically.

question: Whats the very first file a visitor usually reads to understand what a codebase does and how to get started?
expected_answer: It is usually the first document people see; describing what the project does and how to use it.

question: On a brand-new repository, what name does the primary line of development usually get by convention?
expected_answer: It is usually called main or master.

question: What happens to a repositorys full history when you make a local copy of someone elses remote project for the first time?
expected_answer: It downloads a full copy of a remote repository including its entire commit history.

question: When two branches are combined into one commit, where do that commits two parent links point to?
expected_answer: The tips of the two branches being combined.

question: After shelving some unfinished work temporarily, what single command brings those changes back?
expected_answer: git stash pop
